checks.claim: Brake fluid carries the push from the pedal's master cylinder to the caliper pistons, multiplying the force.
checks.why: The pressure is the same through the closed fluid, so the larger caliper piston gets a force multiplied by the area ratio.

sources.title: How do hydraulic brakes work? - Fluid Power World

checks.claim: Vented brake discs have air channels between their two faces that cool them.
checks.why: A ventilated disc has two friction faces separated by vanes that pump air from the hub out through the channels.

sources.title: US4083435A - Brake disc with improved ventilation cooling

checks.claim: Anti-lock brakes pulse the brake pressure many times a second to keep the wheels from locking.
checks.why: Mazda: the valves cut and restore pressure multiple times per second until the car stops; other sources up to about 15 a second. No number used.

sources.title: What Is an Anti-lock Braking System (ABS)? - Mazda USA

checks.claim: Brake lights switch on when the brake pedal is pressed to warn drivers behind.
checks.why: The brake light switch at the pedal arm closes the circuit to the rear lights, signalling following drivers.
